Same weekend, two different economies.

In the U.S., Adobe Analytics projects a record $12.9 billion spent online on Black Friday — up about 9.2% from last year's $11.8 billion. That's the sixth straight record, after $10.8 billion in 2024.

Across the border, the mood is colder. In BCG's 2026 year-end study, Canadians say 62 cents of every Black Friday dollar is going to essentials, not gifts — and nearly nine in ten say they're worried about food and energy costs.

My take: a "record" headline hides who's actually spending. More dollars can just mean steeper prices and more borrowing, not more under the tree. The Canadian number is the honest one — people buying what they need, skipping what they don't.

Which camp are you in this year — splurging, or sticking to essentials? 👇

Source: Adobe Analytics and BCG 2026 Year-End Sales Events Consumer Study (Nov. 2026)
